proposals.title: Observation-only: terminal-capacity saturation is workload-mix intrinsic; no query_execution knob is causally implicated by the verified incumbent
proposals.configuration_cause: None identified in the query_execution knob set. The incumbent already routes every access through an index (idx_scan 23774/s, seq_scan 0.0/s), serves 99.992% of buffer accesses from shared memory (buffer_hit_ratio 0.9999213, blks_read 23.31/s vs blks_hit 296142/s, blks_hit_per_txn 9.28), and selects an actual Index Scan for the sampled point lookup (estimated_rows 1.0, estimated_total_cost 8.45, far below any jit_above_cost threshold, so jit=on cannot be firing). The reported saturation is a property of the closed-loop transaction mix (GetUserTweets = 3449949 of ~3.83M client transactions, ~90%) that consumes 843.5s of the 960s finite terminal budget, not a consequence of a mis-set planner/executor knob.
proposals.mechanism: Closed-loop control: goodput_rps = terminals / weighted-mean client latency. Observed 8 terminals / 249us = 32.1k rps, matching the measured 31.9k rps. The weighted mean is dominated by GetUserTweets (mean 244.5us, p50 157us, p99 2280us, 90% of calls), so the entire terminal budget is one class of cache-resident index lookups. Two structural facts bound what any query_execution knob can do: (1) GetUserTweets is read-only, so it never enqueues on the WAL commit path - wal_write (229.0/s) exactly matches InsertTweet count (38387 in 168.4s = 228.4/s) and wal_bytes_per_txn is 4.77B, i.e. the wal_wait alert is carried by a single sampled waiter (wal_waiting_backends median 0, p95 0, max 1) with 0.134ms average WAL write latency and zero host I/O stall; (2) GetUserTweets adds no physical I/O to remove (9.28 buffer hits/txn, 0.00073 physical reads/txn). What remains is executor/lock-manager micro-stall in the tail (mean 244.5us vs p50 157us, i.e. ~87us of mean is tail), which no allowed knob (jit, random/seq_page_cost, effective_*_size, *_collapse_limit, parallel settings, work_mem, temp_buffers) addresses for a cached single-index path, and which is inside the +-3.5% replicate spread (verified replicates 29762.6 / 30213.6 / 31906.7 rps; GetUserTweets p50 165/169/157us).
proposals.query_effect: No query, plan or access path is changed. The diagnosed statement class (GetUserTweets) already executes as a cached index access path; the sampled plan evidence (Index Scan, cost 8.45, rows 1.0) confirms index usage and no JIT eligibility. The only measurement gap is that the sampled EXPLAIN is for a different statement (SELECT * FROM tweets WHERE id=1) than the budget-dominating class, so no plan mutation is justified on this evidence.
proposals.expected_tps_effect: unchanged: no knob is changed; the incumbent sits at 29762.6-31906.7 rps (median 30213.6) and is expected to remain inside that replicate band.
proposals.expected_latency_effect: unchanged: GetUserTweets p50 ~157us / p99 ~2280us keeps consuming ~0.88 of terminal capacity; the non-dominant classes stay at their measured shares (GetFollowers 0.0514, GetTweetsFromFollowing 0.0367, InsertTweet 0.0223, GetTweet 0.0070).

predictions.rationale: Closed loop identity 8 terminals / 249us mean = 32.1k rps reproduces the measured 31.9k rps; with no change we predict throughput stays within +-5% of the incumbent band 29762.6-31906.7 rps.

p50 157us is a shared-memory index access (buffer_hit_ratio 0.9999213, blks_read_per_txn 0.00073); no allowed knob changes the executor path for this plan. Baseline p50s were 165/169/157us (+-4%), so a 10% tolerance bound is conservative.

p99 2280us (baselines 2451/2486/2280us) is executor/lock-manager micro-stall on hot cached pages; the query_execution knob set contains no lever for that path, so we predict no movement beyond the observed replicate spread.
0.8787 = 843.5s / (8 terminals * 120s); baselines were 0.8798/0.8817/0.8787. Count and mean latency are both unchanged by a no-op, so the fraction stays ~0.88 within +-5%.

Measured 0.1345ms average per WAL write with host_io some/full stall fraction 0.0; the wal_wait alert rests on a single sample (wal_waiting_backends median 0, p95 0, max 1). A genuine WAL-stall mechanism would require an order-of-magnitude higher write latency or sustained waiters, so we predict the mean stays within +-0.5ms.

alternatives.statement: The GetUserTweets tail (p99 2280us, max 27247us) is a WAL commit/fdatasync stall propagated from InsertTweet commits under wal_sync_method=open_datasync and wal_writer_delay=215ms, matching the high-severity wal_wait alert.

The finite terminal budget is consumed by client-side result handling and protocol round trips rather than server execution, as suggested by client_waiting_backends p95=5 of 8 connections and idle_in_transaction p95=3.
The tail comes from physical reads because shared_buffers (53504 pages ~ 437MB) cannot hold the hot set on this 2.16TB host.

cross_domain_requirements: query_execution measurement gap: no EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) exists for the exact GetUserTweets statement, only for SELECT * FROM tweets WHERE id=1 (Index Scan, cost 8.45); plan-level claims about that class must not be made until it is captured.
concurrency_maintenance: confirm commit_delay=671us with commit_siblings=12 is inert at the observed 9-10 backends (guard can never be satisfied), i.e. it cannot be the source of either alert.

memory_storage: if a future round needs more read-path margin, shared_buffers=53504 pages and huge_pages=off are the restart-class levers; current evidence (0.9999213 hit ratio) does not justify them.
proposals.why_exceeds_incumbent: It does not, and this proposal deliberately claims no improvement: knob_changes is empty because the two diagnostic alerts are structural or unsupported by the incumbent's own evidence. client_terminal_saturation is an algebraic consequence of a fixed 90%-dominant transaction class over cached index lookups, and wal_wait is carried by wal_waiting_backends max=1 against 0.1345ms average WAL write latency and zero host I/O stall, while 100% of WAL writes coincide with InsertTweet (229.0/s vs 228.4/s) and GetUserTweets is read-only. Any change inside the allowed query_execution set is bounded by the 87.9% share of a path that has no physical I/O and no spill to remove, i.e. below the +-3.5% replicate noise; proposing one would be an unevidenced gamble. The correct next action is measurement-only: capture EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) and per-wait-event timing for the exact GetUserTweets SQL before any knob is touched.

proposals.title: Observation only: the flagged wal_wait is a single-backend wait below the storage noise floor, while GetUserTweets consumes 87.87% of terminal capacity
proposals.configuration_cause: No incumbent storage setting is causally implicated by the measured evidence. The only settings that could generate the flagged wal_wait are the durability pipeline: wal_sync_method=open_datasync, wal_writer_delay=215 ms, wal_writer_flush_after=367 pages, wal_buffers=637 pages, commit_delay=671 us with commit_siblings=12. Their own telemetry refutes queueing on that path (wal_write_time_per_txn=9.65e-4 ms, wal_sync_time_per_txn=0.0, wal_timing.write_average_ms=0.134, host_io some/full stall fraction=0.0, wal_waiting_backends median=0/p95=0/max=1 out of ~9 backends). commit_delay is moreover inert at this concurrency: it arms only when at least commit_siblings=12 other sessions are in active transactions, and numbackends peaks at 10 (active max 9). shared_buffers=53504 pages (~418 MB) with buffer_hit_ratio=0.999921 and 7.30e-4 blks_read per transaction shows no cache shortfall, and temp_files=temp_bytes=0 rules out spill. Checkpoint/bgwriter are idle, not misconfigured for this load: checkpoints_req=0, checkpoint_write_time=0, checkpoint_sync_time=0, buffers_clean=0.0/s, buffers_checkpoint_per_txn=2.36e-4.
proposals.mechanism: Storage demand in this incumbent is two to four orders of magnitude below device capacity, so the storage layer cannot be the rate limiter. WAL generation is 152.1 kB/s, i.e. 4.77 bytes and 0.0072 WAL writes per transaction; WAL write service time is 0.134 ms per write and 9.65e-4 ms per transaction (about 1e-5 % of wall time per transaction), and no backend ever recorded an fsync (wal_sync=0.0/s, wal_sync_time=0.0, wal_timing.sync_average_ms=null). The buffer path is equally idle: 9.28 buffer hits per transaction at a 0.999921 hit ratio, 7.30e-4 block reads per transaction, and blk_read_time_per_txn=6.65e-6 ms. Writeback is quiescent: buffers_clean=0.0/s, dirty_bytes median 4.28 MB / p95 33.0 MB, writeback_bytes median 0, PSI some/full I/O stall fraction 0.0, io_waiting_backends max 1, wal_waiting_backends max 1. A single instantaneous WALWrite wait on at most one of ~9 backends across 154 samples is below the queueing/sampling noise floor of an 8-terminal closed loop. Meanwhile the client side is the binding resource: GetUserTweets alone consumes 0.8787 of terminal capacity (843.50 s of 8 x 168.44 s = 1347.54 s) at a 157 us median / 244.5 us mean / 593 us p95, and the sum of all transaction-class fractions is ~0.996, i.e. the eight terminals are effectively 100% busy. In a saturation-limited closed loop, throughput equals terminals/latency, so only reductions in client-observed per-transaction latency can raise TPS, and the storage share of that latency is ~1e-6 to 1e-3 ms per transaction. The multi-millisecond tails (GetUserTweets max 27.2 ms, GetTweetsFromFollowing max 31.5 ms, InsertTweet max 54.9 ms) appear across read-only and write classes alike and coincide with zero PSI stall and zero checkpoint write/sync time, so they are not explained by storage service time.

intermediate_metrics.aggregation: mean per transaction over 168.44 s (sync_average_ms reported as null: no sync event recorded)

proposals.query_effect: None. The read path already resolves through shared buffers (EXPLAIN plan evidence: Index Scan on tweets id=1, uses_index=true, estimated_rows=1) at a 0.999921 hit ratio with 9.28 buffer hits per transaction; no plan or access-path change is available inside the storage domain.
proposals.expected_tps_effect: None from this domain. With storage service time per transaction between ~1e-6 ms (block reads) and ~1e-3 ms (WAL writes), and the eight terminals ~99.6% busy, no permitted storage knob can move the incumbent's 31906.7 rps in the next round.
proposals.expected_latency_effect: None attributable to storage. The 157 us p50 / 244.5 us mean of GetUserTweets is parse, plan, buffer access and round-trip; the storage component is less than 0.001% of that latency. InsertTweet's p99 of 3336 us is likewise not sync-dominated, since wal_sync_time is zero and host I/O stalls are zero.

predictions.rationale: The class consumes 0.8787 of terminal capacity (843.50 s of 1347.54 s) at a 157 us median while its storage cost is ~6.65e-6 ms of block read time and zero temp bytes; no storage knob in the allowed set can shift this fraction by 3 points.

Observed 9.65e-4 ms per transaction with write_average_ms=0.134 and PSI io stall fraction 0.0; the WAL write path has no queue to relieve, so no storage-side reconfiguration should change it by more than 25%.

The flagged wait is a single instantaneous sample: median 0.0, p95 0.0, max 1 out of ~9 backends. Reconfiguring the WAL/commit pipeline cannot remove a wait that is not present beyond the noise floor, so the max should not move by 1 or more backends.

InsertTweet p99 is 3336 us on 0.0072 WAL writes and zero recorded fsync time per transaction; the commit durability path is not the tail driver, so its p99 should not move by 10% from any permitted storage change.

alternatives.statement: A slow durable flush (fsync/open_datasync) on the commit path inflates InsertTweet's tail and forces backends to queue on WAL.
Background-writer or checkpoint writeback bursts stall readers and produce the 17-31 ms maxima seen across read-only classes.
shared_buffers is too small for the twitter working set, so the read path pays buffer misses that dominate GetUserTweets latency.

cross_domain_requirements: query_execution: attribute the 244.5 us GetUserTweets mean and 2280 us p99 to parse/plan/round-trip cost, since storage contributes <0.001% of per-transaction latency here.
concurrency_maintenance: with eight terminals ~99.6% busy, validate the terminal/admission model before any server-side micro-tuning; throughput is terminal-time-bound, not resource-bound.
measurement: keep track_io_timing and track_wal_io_timing enabled so wal_timing and host_io evidence remain available to falsify any storage hypothesis in the next round.
proposals.why_exceeds_incumbent: It does not claim a TPS gain; it claims the incumbent storage configuration is already non-binding and left untouched, which strictly dominates any unfalsifiable storage edit. Every storage path shows >=99.9% idle headroom: wal_write_time_per_txn 9.65e-4 ms, wal_sync_time_per_txn 0, blk_read_time_per_txn 6.65e-6 ms, checkpoint write+sync time 0, buffers_clean 0/s, PSI full/some io stall 0.0, temp_bytes 0. Acting on the wal_wait alert would spend measurement budget on a no-op while risking a real regression (e.g. enlarging wal_buffers/shared_buffers at 418 MB with a 0.999921 hit ratio, or trading commit-path latency for a group-commit benefit that cannot materialise because commit_delay needs >=12 concurrent sibling transactions and only ~9 backends exist).

proposals.title: Observation-only: No configuration cause for GetUserTweets dominance
proposals.configuration_cause: No configuration cause identified. The incumbent's autovacuum, WAL, and concurrency settings are within healthy ranges, and there are zero lock waits, zero conflicts, and a 99.99% buffer hit ratio. The critical transaction GetUserTweets is the most frequent transaction, not anomalously slow.
proposals.mechanism: The terminal capacity fraction of GetUserTweets is 87.9% because it represents 3.45 million of the 3.8 million total transactions, not because of excessive per-transaction latency (p50=157us, p99=2280us). The overall system is healthy: no lock waits, no deadlocks, negligible WAL waits (max 1 backend), and no I/O stalls. Therefore, no knob change is justified.
proposals.expected_tps_effect: No change expected; throughput remains around 31,900 rps.
proposals.expected_latency_effect: No change expected; overall p95 remains around 646us.

predictions.rationale: No intervention is applied; the incumbent is already healthy and the dominant transaction is frequent but not anomalous. Throughput is expected to remain stable.

alternatives.statement: Stale statistics from infrequent autovacuum analyze cause suboptimal query plans for GetUserTweets.
Long wal_writer_delay causes occasional WAL flushes that indirectly delay read transactions via I/O contention.

proposals.why_exceeds_incumbent: No change is proposed; therefore no improvement over the incumbent is claimed. This observation-only proposal avoids unnecessary configuration churn.
